input.spec:
Audit pull request https://github.com/RankOneLabs/oakridge/pull/791 (branch cohort/automatic-execution-lifecycle/73c9f2) in repository oakridge. This is an isolated verification run of the committed development definition, not feature work: its only purpose is real analysis, plan, brief, build_result and assessment artifacts for observation to capture and grade. The analysis reports at least three separate findings about this spec, each a distinct observation. Produce exactly one cohort, named audit, with two tasks. T1: a run's launch config carries grading_enabled, off when missing, through the ordered launch delivery (oakridge-dbos/src/domain/run-config.ts, oakridge-dbos/src/adapters/observation-mapping.ts). T2: settlement of an evaluation execution is fenced to the exact current claim, and completion appends its observation in one transaction (observation/src/storage/execution-store.ts, observation/src/grading/worker.ts).
The operator authorizes this audit path: the builder publishes the existing PR #791 as its pr artifact instead of pushing or opening one. No brief may add a further operator choice or confirmation. The builder must not edit files, create commits, push, open or update any pull request, merge, reset a database or deploy. Its worktree starts from epic/grade-pray, the base of pull request #791, so it first checks out the head of branch cohort/automatic-execution-lifecycle/73c9f2 locally (git checkout --detach origin/cohort/automatic-execution-lifecycle/73c9f2) and inspects that commit, runs bun install if needed and then bun run --filter observation test once, and publishes build_result with the commit it inspected as head_sha and the actual test counts and output. A test that cannot run is a known issue, never a reason to invent results. It then publishes the existing pull request https://github.com/RankOneLabs/oakridge/pull/791 as the pr artifact, with branch cohort/automatic-execution-lifecycle/73c9f2.
The assessor assesses that same commit without changing anything. Give at least one finding per task. Every finding cites at least one file as path:start-end at that commit, for example observation/src/grading/worker.ts:20-40, and cites test output separately as test or output evidence. Report the builder's test run as test_evidence.
Keep the spec, tasks, plan and brief short; there are no ambiguous requirements to resolve.
input.title: Automatic grading lifecycle audit

risks.mitigation: The builder must publish the exact command output and actual pass/fail/skip counts, treating an unavailable environment as a known issue as the specification already directs.
risks.description: The observation suite contains PostgreSQL integration tests, so local infrastructure or credentials may prevent execution even though the test script is valid (observation/package.json:6-8; observation/tests/execution-lifecycle.test.ts:204-239).

risks.mitigation: Record the detached checkout SHA in build_result and require the assessor to use that SHA; before checkout, compare the local remote-tracking ref with PR status. At analysis time both resolve to 10cddc5ff69124002c485b011dba5d34ebe6de75.
risks.description: The PR head branch can move between stages, which could otherwise make builder and assessor inspect different commits.

body.summary: The specification is short, internally complete, and implementable without an operator choice. Live PR metadata and local refs agree that PR #791 targets epic/grade-pray from cohort/automatic-execution-lifecycle/73c9f2 at 10cddc5ff69124002c485b011dba5d34ebe6de75. Repository evidence independently supports T1 defaulting/preservation and ordered launch mapping, plus T2 exact-claim fencing and atomic completion/observation append. No specification update is needed; the mandated observation test remains the runtime qualification to report honestly.

findings.description: The audit target is coherent: gated PR status reports PR #791 open with base epic/grade-pray, head cohort/automatic-execution-lifecycle/73c9f2, and head SHA 10cddc5ff69124002c485b011dba5d34ebe6de75; the local origin refs resolve to the same base and head. This makes the specified detached-checkout audit path concrete.

T1 has direct implementation evidence: RunConfig names grading_enabled as a boolean and parseRunConfig defaults only an absent value to false while rejecting a supplied non-boolean (oakridge-dbos/src/domain/run-config.ts:7-11,21-41). Focused tests cover omitted, explicit, and malformed choices (oakridge-dbos/tests/run-config.test.ts:56-83).

T1 also has a distinct delivery observation: MappingInput carries the launch-specific committed run_config, and launched events emit the exact committed config beside input, map no config to null, and reject malformed committed config (oakridge-dbos/src/adapters/observation-mapping.ts:14-18,42-49). Tests distinguish on, off, none, and malformed delivery (oakridge-dbos/tests/observation-mapping.test.ts:50-65).

T2 claim settlement is fenced by execution id, claimed status, lease owner, claim attempt, and an unexpired lease under a row lock (observation/src/storage/execution-store.ts:193-215). The worker passes the same claim through request marking and both success/failure settlement paths (observation/src/grading/worker.ts:71-100), while integration cases exercise expired, reclaimed, and old-attempt claims (observation/tests/execution-lifecycle.test.ts:299-320).

T2 atomicity is separately visible: completeExecution opens one withTenant transaction, rechecks the fence, marks the execution and provider attempt completed, inserts grade_observation, and returns only after the unit commits (observation/src/storage/execution-store.ts:227-253). The integration test deliberately causes observation insertion to fail and verifies neither completion nor answer persists, then verifies both persist on valid input (observation/tests/execution-lifecycle.test.ts:226-239).

requirements.description: Produce exactly one cohort named audit with two tasks, preserve at least three distinct analysis findings, and keep the downstream artifacts concise.
Audit grading_enabled through RunConfig parsing/default-off behavior and exact ordered launch delivery using the named oakridge-dbos files.
Audit exact-current-claim settlement fencing and transactional completion plus grade observation append using the named observation files.

Detach to the existing PR head, make no source/PR/deployment changes, run the observation test command once, report actual output/counts and inspected SHA, then publish existing PR #791 rather than opening or updating one.
Assess the builder-inspected commit without mutation, provide at least one path:line-range finding per task, cite test/output evidence separately, and report the builder run as test_evidence.

source_spec_refs: Audit purpose and fixed one-cohort/two-task topology
T1: grading_enabled default and ordered launch delivery
T2: exact-claim fencing and atomic observation append
Builder: detached checkout, one observation test run, build_result, and existing PR publication
Assessor: same-commit review, per-task findings, and separate test/output evidence
